name: interactive-test
title: Interactive Hardware Validation with .test()
description: All 16 NovaMP v1.0 classes support .test() — an interactive REPL wizard that validates hardware before writing application code.

pattern.workflow: When wiring a new module, ALWAYS run its .test() first
pattern.rationale: Verifies pinout, power, and basic functionality before investing time in application code

code:
# Generic pattern — works for any NovaMP class
from <module> import <Class>
<Class>.test()

# Example 1: LED
from led import LED
LED.test()
# Prompts: pin number, then runs on/off/blink/fade/breathe sequence

# Example 2: HCSR04
from hcsr04 import HCSR04
HCSR04.test()
# Prompts: trig pin, echo pin, then loops printing distance

# Example 3: WiFi
from wifi import WiFi
WiFi.test()
# Scans networks → prompts SSID/password → connects → prints IP

best_practices: Always run .test() before writing application code — verifies hardware
If .test() fails, do NOT proceed — fix wiring first
Use the .test() prompts to discover the right GPIO for your wiring
After .test() succeeds, use the prompts' defaults as starting points for your code
.test() is interactive — requires REPL connection. Cannot be called from main.py directly.
esp32_notes: All .test() methods use input() — requires active REPL connection via mpremote/Thonny
.test() blocks the main thread — do not call from main.py without redirection
Most .test() methods use try/finally to release PWM resources even on Ctrl+C

common_mistakes.mistake: Skipping .test() and jumping straight to application code
common_mistakes.fix: Run .test() first — saves debugging time on wiring issues
.test() is for interactive REPL only. Use .help() to learn API, then write app code.
Most .test() methods auto-deinit on Ctrl+C. If they don't, manually call .deinit().
